the reduction of serum uc-oc in older patients who received MK-4 is more efficient when they have the A allele.

the effect of GGCX polymorphisms on vitamin K2 (MK-4)-mediated reduction of serum ucOc in postmenopausal osteoporosis patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GGCX genotype does not affect the response of bone turnover markers after 3 months of treatment of MK-4.
GGCX gene may have an effect on the reduction of uc-OC in the elderly postmenopausal group, however, it is not clear whether it affects other bone turnover markers or not.
GGCX polymorphisms do not influence the reduction of uc OC, beta-CTX or P1NP in postmenopausal osteoporotic women after treatment with MK-4.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the “GGCX” gene polymorphism is associated with the response of “undercarboxylated-osteocalcin (uc-OC)” to vitamin K2 treatment.
GGCX polymorphisms might be one of the factors that affect the response of serum ucOC to vitamin K2 supplementation in the elderly women.
menatetrenon treatment is beneficial to reduce bone resorption and increase bone formation in postmenopausal osteoporotic women.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GGCX gene might play a role in the response of serum ucOC to menatetrenones in the older population.
GGCX polymorphisms may influence vitamin K2 response on bone health in postmenopausal older women.
